name: Nucleo-F103RB (official ST board)

button.note: Blue USER button B1, with an onboard pull-up; reads LOW when pressed. The black button is RESET

buses.i2c: I2C1: SCL PB8 (D15) / SDA PB9 (D14), the two pins at the top-right corner of the Arduino header
buses.spi: SPI1: SCK PA5 (D13) / MISO PA6 (D12) / MOSI PA7 (D11) / CS usually PB6 (D10). Note that SCK and the onboard LED share the same pin, PA5
buses.uart: Serial (USART2): TX PA2 / RX PA3, wired straight to the onboard ST-Link's USB virtual COM port, so you can see output as soon as you plug in USB; USART1: TX PA9 (D8) / RX PA10 (D2) for external modules

power: 3.3V logic. Pins with an ADC function (PA0-PA7, PB0, PB1, PC0-PC5) are not 5V-tolerant; most other I/O pins are 5V-tolerant (FT). The board is powered over USB; the 5V header pin can supply about 300mA and the 3V3 pin about 300mA (more headroom than the Blue Pill). You can also feed 7-12V into VIN
flash_how: The top half of the board is a built-in ST-Link V2-1 programmer. One USB cable (mini-B, not micro) to your computer handles flashing, power and serial all at once; nothing else to buy. pio run -t upload flashes directly; LD1 blinks red/green while flashing. A USB drive named NODE_F103RB also appears on your computer, and dragging a .bin onto it flashes too. The serial monitor pio device monitor shows Serial output directly
gotchas: The onboard LED LD2 is on PA5 (D13) and is active-high, the opposite of the Blue Pill's PC13. PA5 is also SPI1 SCK, so the LED flickers when you use SPI; that's normal
On the F103, PA5 has no timer channel, so analogWrite(PA5) produces no PWM. For a breathing LED use D3, D5, D6, D9, etc.

D0/D1 (PA3/PA2) on the Arduino header are disconnected by default (solder bridges SB62/SB63 are open), because USART2 is routed to the ST-Link virtual COM port. Serial output over USB works fine, but there's no signal on the D0/D1 header pins (verify)
The USER button on PC13 reads LOW when pressed. pinMode with INPUT is enough (the board has a pull-up); if (digitalRead(PC13) == LOW) means pressed
A4/A5 (PC1/PC0) are not I2C pins. The UNO habit of using A4/A5 as SDA/SCL doesn't work here; use D14/D15 for I2C
PC14/PC15 are taken by the 32.768kHz crystal and PC13 is the button; don't use these three as ordinary I/O

The Morpho headers (the two long rows on the sides, CN7/CN10) expose dozens more pins than the Arduino header. Their names are chip pin names like PB12, PC10, which are harder to mix up than D numbers
The USB port is mini-B, not the same as a phone cable; get a mini-B cable
The board's 5V comes from USB (jumper JP5 in its default U5V position). Power big loads (servos, LED strips) separately, not from the board

left.name: IOREF
left.note: Tells shields this board runs 3.3V logic; wired to 3.3V

left.name: RESET
left.note: Pull to ground to reset, same as pressing the black RESET button

left.name: GND
left.note: Every ground must be tied together

left.name: VIN
left.note: External 7-12V supply input, for when you're not on USB

left.name: A0 / PA0
left.note: Use this to read the potentiometer

left.name: A4 / PC1
left.note: Not an I2C pin (unlike the UNO)

left.name: A5 / PC0
left.note: Not an I2C pin (unlike the UNO)

right.name: AREF
right.note: ADC reference voltage, wired to AVDD; normally leave it alone

right.name: D13 / PA5
right.note: Onboard LED LD2, active-high. Also the SPI clock; the two share this pin

right.name: D8 / PA9
right.note: Connect to an external serial module's RX

right.name: D5 / PB4
right.note: JTAG pin by default; released automatically once you call pinMode

right.name: D3 / PB3
right.note: JTAG pin by default; released automatically once you call pinMode

right.name: D2 / PA10
right.note: Connect to an external serial module's TX

right.name: D1 / PA2
right.note: Taken by the ST-Link virtual COM port; no signal on the header pin by default (verify)

bottom.name: PC13
bottom.note: Blue USER button, LOW when pressed. On Morpho header CN7

bottom.name: PC14
bottom.note: Taken by the 32.768kHz crystal; don't use as GPIO

bottom.name: PB12
bottom.note: Morpho only, 5V-tolerant; great for buttons and relays

bottom.name: PA13
bottom.note: SWDIO, wired to the onboard ST-Link; leave it alone
